cls: Botulinum toxin type A (acetylcholine release inhibitor / neuromuscular blocker)

summary: OnabotulinumtoxinA (BOTOX) is a botulinum toxin type A that blocks acetylcholine release at cholinergic nerve terminals, producing local chemical denervation. It is given by injection for chronic migraine, overactive bladder and neurogenic detrusor overactivity, upper/lower limb spasticity, cervical dystonia, blepharospasm, strabismus, severe axillary hyperhidrosis, and (BOTOX Cosmetic) facial lines. It carries a boxed warning for distant spread of toxin effect causing potentially life-threatening dysphagia and breathing difficulty. Units are product-specific and not interchangeable with other botulinum toxin products.
indications: Overactive bladder with urge urinary incontinence, urgency and frequency in adults inadequately responsive to or intolerant of an anticholinergic
Urinary incontinence due to detrusor overactivity associated with a neurologic condition (neurogenic detrusor overactivity)
Prophylaxis of headaches in adults with chronic migraine (>=15 days/month, headaches lasting >=4 hours/day)
Spasticity in adult and pediatric patients (upper and lower limb)
Severe axillary hyperhidrosis inadequately managed by topical agents
Moderate-to-severe glabellar, lateral canthal (crow's feet) and forehead lines (BOTOX Cosmetic)

100 Units total, as 0.5 mL (5 U) injections across 20 intradetrusor sites

dosage.n: Limit dose to least effective; lower dose if naive

dosage.d: 20 Units total = 4 U (0.1 mL) IM into each of 5 sites
dosage.t: Re-treat no more often than every 3 months
dosage.n: Cosmetic label is separate from therapeutic BOTOX

admin: For injection only by trained clinicians; route varies by indication (IM, intradetrusor, intradermal)
Reconstitute each vacuum-dried vial only with sterile preservative-free 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection
Use within 24 hours after reconstitution; store reconstituted product refrigerated (2-8 C)
BOTOX Units are specific to the assay and NOT interchangeable with other botulinum toxin products
Have epinephrine and resuscitation equipment available for possible anaphylaxis
moa: OnabotulinumtoxinA binds to receptors on cholinergic motor nerve terminals, is internalized, and cleaves SNAP-25, a protein required for docking and release of acetylcholine-containing vesicles. This inhibits acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, producing local chemical denervation and muscle relaxation. In the bladder it is thought to relax the detrusor; in chronic migraine it is theorized to act on peripheral pain pathways. Effect is reversible as new nerve terminals sprout and junctional transmission is re-established over months.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any botulinum toxin product or formulation component
Infection at the proposed injection site(s)
For bladder injection: urinary tract infection at time of treatment
For bladder injection: urinary retention / post-void residual >200 mL in patients not routinely performing clean intermittent self-catheterization
relative: Pre-existing neuromuscular disorders (myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, ALS) - increased risk of systemic effects
monitor: Concomitant aminoglycosides or other neuromuscular blocking agents
Recent or planned use of another botulinum toxin product

preg: There are no adequate human data. Animal studies showed reduced fetal weight, skeletal effects and abortions at clinically relevant doses associated with maternal toxicity. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: There is no information on the presence of onabotulinumtoxinA in human or animal milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production. Weigh developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is provided. Pharmacokinetics in renal impairment have not been characterized; the drug acts locally with low systemic exposure at therapeutic doses.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is provided. Pharmacokinetics in hepatic impairment have not been characterized.

major: Aminoglycoside antibiotics and other agents interfering with neuromuscular transmission (curare-like nondepolarizing blockers) - may potentiate the effect of BOTOX; observe closely
Other botulinum neurotoxin products - co-administration or use within a few months may exacerbate excessive neuromuscular weakness (not studied)
moderate: Anticholinergic drugs - may potentiate systemic anticholinergic effects
minor: Other agents that may impair neuromuscular transmission - use caution
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction described in labeling.

serious: Distant spread of toxin effect (boxed warning)
Dysphagia - can be severe and prolonged, requiring feeding support
emergency: Generalized muscle weakness from systemic spread

monitoring: Signs of distant toxin spread: dysphagia, dysphonia, dysarthria, ptosis, diplopia, generalized weakness, breathing difficulty (hours to weeks after injection)
For bladder indications: post-void residual urine volume, ability to void, urinary tract infection
Patients with neuromuscular disease or respiratory/swallowing compromise - closer observation for systemic effects
Clinical response and timing of symptom recurrence to guide re-treatment
counsel: Seek immediate medical care for trouble swallowing, speaking or breathing, or generalized muscle weakness - these can occur hours to weeks after injection
BOTOX Units are not interchangeable with other botulinum toxin products
Tell your clinician about any nerve/muscle disease, breathing or swallowing problems, prior botulinum toxin reactions, surgery, or pregnancy/breastfeeding
For bladder injection you may need to self-catheterize if you cannot empty your bladder; report UTI symptoms
The effect is temporary; repeat treatment is usually needed, generally no sooner than every 3 months
pk: Maximum effect approximately 1-2 weeks after injection
Acts locally; systemic PK not characterized at therapeutic doses
Refrigerate vials 2-8 C; reconstituted product 2-8 C, use within 24 h
pearls: Boxed warning: effects may spread from the injection area producing botulinum toxin symptoms (dysphagia, breathing difficulty) - reported hours to weeks later and can be fatal
Potency Units are specific to BOTOX and cannot be compared to or converted into units of any other botulinum toxin product
Risk of distant spread is probably greatest in children treated for spasticity but can occur in adults with predisposing conditions
Re-injection should generally be no sooner than every 12 weeks (3 months)
missed: Not a daily medication - there is no missed-dose concept. Repeat treatment is given when the effect of the prior injection has diminished, but generally no sooner than every 12 weeks (3 months). Schedule re-treatment at the appropriate interval.
overdose: Signs of overdose are likely not present immediately after injection. If excessive dose, accidental injection or oral ingestion is suspected, monitor the person for several weeks for systemic muscular weakness (generalized weakness, ptosis, diplopia, swallowing/speech difficulty, respiratory compromise), which may be local or distant. Institute supportive care including respiratory support as needed; consider hospitalization. In symptomatic systemic botulinum toxicity, early administration of botulinum antitoxin may be beneficial.
